guides.title: How Much Does a Nanny Cost in Orlando, FL? (2026)
guides.desc: Hourly rates for nannies and babysitters in Orlando, what drives the price, and the taxes families owe when they hire a nanny.
guides.html:
Typical rates

WhoTypical rate in OrlandoSource
Nanny$20.79–$26.36/hrCare.com, Nov 2026
Babysitter$18.78–$27.63/hrCare.com, Nov 2026
Childcare workers (all settings), median wage$15.00/hr (mean $15.81)BLS OEWS, May 2025
Florida minimum wage$15.00/hr since Sep 30, 2026Florida Constitution, Art. X §24

What changes the price

  • Number and ages of children: families usually add $1–$2/hour per extra child.
  • Experience, CPR/first-aid and education in early childhood.
  • Driving: a nanny who drives the kids usually costs more.
  • Languages: bilingual nannies are in demand in Orlando.
  • Full-time vs. occasional: full-time nannies often agree on a weekly salary.

A simple monthly estimate

A full-time nanny at $22/hour for 40 hours a week costs about $3,800 a month before taxes ($22 × 40 × 52 ÷ 12).

Taxes families owe

In 2026, if you pay a nanny $3,000 or more in cash wages in the year, you withhold 7.65% (Social Security and Medicare) from their pay and pay the same 7.65% yourself. If you pay $1,000 or more in a calendar quarter, federal unemployment tax (FUTA) and Florida reemployment tax also apply. You report it all on Schedule H. Florida has no state income tax. See how to hire a household employee in Florida.

Find a nanny in Orlando
faq: How much is a full-time nanny in Orlando per month?
About $3,600 to $4,600 a month for 40 hours a week at the typical Orlando range of $20.79–$26.36/hour (Care.com, November 2026), before employer taxes.
Do I have to pay taxes for my nanny in Florida?

If you pay them $3,000 or more in 2026, yes: Social Security and Medicare (7.65% each side). Florida has no state income tax, but Florida reemployment tax applies if you pay $1,000 or more in a quarter.

guides.title: How to Hire a Household Employee in Florida (2026 Guide)
guides.desc: Nanny tax, minimum wage, Florida reemployment tax and the paperwork families need when they hire a nanny, housekeeper or cook in Florida.
guides.html:
1. Is the worker your employee?

If you control what work is done and how it's done, the worker is generally your household employee — a nanny or housekeeper on your schedule, for example. If the worker runs their own business, brings their own tools and offers services to the public, they're generally self-employed (IRS Publication 926).

2. Pay at least minimum wage

The Florida minimum wage is $15.00/hour since September 30, 2026, and will be adjusted for inflation every year from 2027.

3. Federal taxes (the "nanny tax")

  • Social Security and Medicare: if you pay one household employee $3,000 or more in cash wages in 2026, you withhold 6.2% + 1.45% from their pay and pay the same amount yourself.
  • FUTA: if you pay $1,000 or more to household employees in any calendar quarter, you owe federal unemployment tax (6% on the first $7,000 per employee, usually reduced by state credit).
  • You report these on Schedule H with your Form 1040 and give the employee a Form W-2.
  • Wages paid to workers under 18 don't count for Social Security and Medicare unless household work is their main occupation.

4. Florida taxes

  • No state income tax to withhold.
  • Florida reemployment tax: applies if you pay $1,000 or more in a calendar quarter for domestic services; it's charged on the first $7,000 per employee per year, at 2.7% for new employers (Florida Department of Revenue).

5. Put it in writing

Agree in writing on hours, duties, pay, overtime, paid time off and how either side ends the arrangement.

Sources: IRS Publication 926 (2026) · Florida Department of Revenue — reemployment tax · Florida Constitution, Art. X §24.
faq: What is the nanny tax threshold for 2026?
$3,000 in cash wages paid to one household employee in the year (IRS Publication 926).
Do I need to withhold Florida income tax?
No. Florida has no state income tax.
